message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on freeways, 35 mph on expressways, 25 mph on city streets (unless posted).
• “No speed limit” roads allow drivers to set a safe speed. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The law applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles (helmet required). | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• On a four‑way stop, the first vehicle to arrive has the right of way. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus’s stop sign is retracted. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers.
• Overtake only when it is safe and legal. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a stop sign.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (2 / 32 in. minimum).
• Mirrors must be properly adjusted. | | **Traffic Violations & Penalties** | • Minor infractions: fines, points on license.
• Major infractions: higher fines, license suspension, possible jail.
• Points accumulate; 12 points in 12 months can lead to license suspension. | | **Special Cases** | • **Texas DOT “No‑Stop” Law**: Drivers may proceed through a green light without stopping if the intersection is clear.
• **High‑way “No‑Stop” Law**: Drivers may proceed through a green light on a highway without stopping if the intersection is clear. | ### How to Find More Detailed Information 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.HTM 2. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Offers driver handbooks, FAQs, and enforcement updates. *Website:* https://www.dps.texas.gov/ 3. **Local County or City Ordinances** – May contain additional rules (e.g., specific speed limits, parking restrictions). Check your local municipality’s website. 4. **Legal Resources** – If you need legal interpretation or representation, consult a Texas attorney or the Texas Bar Association. --- **Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas** - Always keep your seat belt fastened and ensure passengers do the same. - Avoid using your phone while driving; use hands‑free if necessary. - Observe posted speed limits and adjust for weather or road conditions. - Be mindful of school buses and pedestrian crossings. - Keep your vehicle in good mechanical condition—regularly check tires, brakes, and lights. Feel free to let me know if you’d like more specific details on any of these topics!
